correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=2 and real c>1, all primal vertices are independently characterized by high/low subset patterns; each polar facet is a product of two orthogonal simplices. The exact facet volume and support-plane height give formula (1) after summing over all 2^m-2 facets. The exponential/beta integral gives the primal volume. A standalone script verifies 177492 exact-rational support/identity assertions and 18 independent hull volumes; the infinite proof is analytic, not experimental.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same result could be expressed as the intrinsic volume of the weighted zero-sum complete-directed-edge configuration with vertices proportional to e_i-c e_j. The closest inspected root-polytope constructions use e_i-e_j or signed unit vectors; their stated theorems do not evaluate the c-dependent volume. In particular, at c>1 opposite ordered-pair vertices do not form negatives, so reducing to an ordinary symmetric type-A root polytope is not justified.

originality.rationale: Kazakov (arXiv:2606.02087v1, Section 5) explicitly leaves the dual-volume problem for further study. Its accessible text computes the primal fraction and basic faces but not the evaluated polar-volume formula. The 2025 root-polytope article works with unweighted roots, and the 1992 dual-volume article provides general machinery rather than an identified instance of the present evaluated family. Targeted scientific and mathematical-record comparisons found no covering statement, subject to unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: The entire text of Filliman (1992) was not available; possible specialized examples cannot be fully excluded.
An unindexed computation of weighted complete-directed-root polytopes might express the same volume in a different normalization.
Search results and historical claim comparisons do not mathematically prove global uniqueness or priority.

value.rationale: The originating 2026 article explicitly proposes investigating the dual-polytope volume; this theorem computes that previously unavailable natural geometric invariant in all dimensions, for the original trisection and arbitrary real ratio. The facet product decomposition provides structural understanding and yields the affine-invariant Santaló volume product for the entire family. This is more than an arbitrary finite table or a reparameterization of the known primal volume.
